[&amp;_summary]:text-xl"><span aria-hidden="true" data-article-top="true" class="absolute top-0 left-0 size-px"></span><p>When the SpaceXSI Sales team first adopted <a href="/bot">Grok Bot</a>, individual reps built their own Bots to research accounts, prepare for meetings, and manage their pipelines. This presented an opportunity to bring together the best of what everyone was building and make it available to the whole team.</p><p>We began creating Shared Bots, each specializing in a role that already exists in our Sales organization. The people who know each job best help build and maintain the Bot, so everyone benefits from their expertise and works from the same up-to-date business knowledge. And as we improve a Bot, everyone who uses it benefits, without having to update their own setup.</p><p>We&#x27;ve started with three Shared Bots, each responsible for a different part of the deal cycle.</p><ul>
<li><strong>Account Intel Bot</strong> helps reps identify prospects, prepare for customer conversations, and keep Salesforce up to date.</li>
<li><strong>Quote Bot</strong> generates pricing proposals and prepares order forms using CPQ tools.</li>
<li><strong>Deal Bot</strong> helps our Deal Desk team review non-standard terms and approve deals.</li>
</ul><p>Each brings its own expertise to the process, allowing us to delegate larger parts of the deal cycle while keeping people focused on customers and the decisions that need their judgment.</p><figure class="not-prose my-12 lg:-mx-12"><div class="bg-card overflow-hidden rounded-2xl"><div class="grid"><div class="col-start-1 row-start-1 dark:hidden"><span class="flex h-full grow"><span role="button" aria-label="Image Preview" class="h-full w-full cursor-pointer"><img alt="How the SpaceXSI Sales team uses Shared Bots to automate the deal cycle: Account Intel Bot handles account research and follow-up, Quote Bot prepares pricing and order forms, and Deal Bot reviews special terms and approvals" class="w-full" loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="object-fit:contain;background:radial-gradient(at 0 0,#ffffff,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 0,#fbf9fa,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 0,#f6f6f8,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 0,#fbf9fa,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 50%,#ffffff,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 50%,#ffffff,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 50%,#f4f2f1,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 50%,#ffffff,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 100%,#ffffff,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 100%,#ffffff,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 100%,#f2f2f4,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 100%,#ffffff,#00000000 50%);width:100%;aspect-ratio:1.4414414414414414" srcSet="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=640,f=auto/v1/website/sales-bot-diagram-light-6-b66d2e51.png 640w,

https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=6016,f=auto/v1/website/sales-bot-diagram-dark-6-5f6bb3a4.png 6016w" src="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,f=auto/v1/website/sales-bot-diagram-dark-6-5f6bb3a4.png"/></span></span></div></div></div></figure><h2 id="how-we-think-about-shared-bots"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#how-we-think-about-shared-bots">How we think about Shared Bots</a></h2><p>Shared Bots are a new way to organize work around superintelligence. They take on defined roles that serve entire teams, which requires careful decisions about what they know, what they can do, and when people need to step in.</p><p>Each Shared Bot needs to understand the systems it operates and the business rules it follows. We give them this knowledge through shared skills and connections to our internal sources of truth, keeping everyone on the same up-to-date rules. When a process changes or we find a better way to perform a task, we can update the Shared Bot once for everyone.</p><p>Shared Bots also need limits on what they can do. They act with each user&#x27;s permissions, with additional restrictions on sensitive actions. We&#x27;ve built rate limits to prevent unintended changes at scale and reserved certain actions for specialist Shared Bots. A sales rep, for example, cannot use Quote Bot to approve their own discount.</p><p>We also set boundaries on when Shared Bots can act independently. For now, we require human review whenever we can&#x27;t clearly define the criteria for a decision, or when a shared Bot prepares customer-facing communications. As we measure the quality of their work and gain confidence in their decisions, we expect to give our Shared Bots more responsibility.</p><h2 id="account-intel-bot-handles-sales-prep-and-follow-up"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#account-intel-bot-handles-sales-prep-and-follow-up">Account Intel Bot handles sales prep and follow-up</a></h2><p>Our Account Intel Bot helps sales reps identify promising accounts, prepare for meetings, and manage their pipelines. Every rep has a private conversation with the same Shared Bot, which draws on shared company knowledge and works with each rep&#x27;s permissions.</p><p>Our GTM engineering team started by having Grok Bot analyze Salesforce activity logs to identify the most valuable work to automate. That showed us that reps were spending a lot of time updating opportunities after customer calls. We gave Account Intel the tools to make those updates and taught it the business rules for when and how to do so.</p><p>Proactivity is another principle we think is important for Shared Bots. Account Intel can prepare a briefing based on account history before a customer meeting. Afterward, it can read the Gong transcript, identify and make the necessary Salesforce updates, and draft a follow-up email for the rep to review.</p><p>Reps can schedule these workflows to run automatically, so much of the preparation and follow-up happens without a separate request.</p><figure class="not-prose my-12 lg:-mx-12"><div class="bg-card overflow-hidden rounded-2xl"><span class="flex h-full grow"><span role="button" aria-label="Image Preview" class="h-full w-full cursor-pointer"><img alt="Account Intel Bot summarizing next steps from a customer conversation and updating the Salesforce opportunity and account plan" class="w-full" loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="object-fit:contain;background:radial-gradient(at 0 0,#c5b8c1,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 0,#d4b9b5,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 0,#d3c4c0,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 0,#cab7b4,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 50%,#cba29c,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 50%,#f7dfdb,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 50%,#e9d6d3,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 50%,#f2dcd7,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 100%,#c7a7a6,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 100%,#f9eae7,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 100%,#f2e8e5,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 100%,#f7eae6,#00000000 50%);width:100%;aspect-ratio:1.537117903930131" srcSet="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=640,f=auto/v1/website/account-intel-01f2079e.png 640w,

Quote Bot inputs the quotes in Salesforce and presents them side by side in the Grok Bot app, so the rep can compare options before choosing one without having to go into the CPQ tool.</p><p>Quote Bot also manages the steps required to turn a quote into an order form. It submits quotes for approval, tracks their status, and routes exceptions to Deal Bot (more on this below). Once a quote is approved, Quote Bot can generate the order form in Ironclad, download the executable contract, and draft an email for the rep to send to the customer. The rep can complete much of this process in one conversation, rather than moving between systems and waiting for updates from other teams.</p><p>We built Quote Bot to handle this work without giving up control over important decisions. Before changing anything in Salesforce, it shows the rep a preview and asks for confirmation. It also operates with the rep&#x27;s own permissions, so approvals and exceptions that require Deal Desk authority stay with Deal Desk.</p><figure class="not-prose my-12 lg:-mx-12"><div class="bg-card overflow-hidden rounded-2xl"><span class="flex h-full grow"><span role="button" aria-label="Image Preview" class="h-full w-full cursor-pointer"><img alt="Quote Bot presenting three side-by-side Salesforce quote options for the same account" class="w-full" loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="object-fit:contain;background:radial-gradient(at 0 0,#d4a4af,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 0,#ffbeb5,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 0,#fccbbe,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 0,#ffbdb3,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 50%,#cc9b9a,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 50%,#f4e3df,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 50%,#dbe0e0,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 50%,#ebe1e3,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 100%,#c59697,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 100%,#fceee8,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 100%,#dddede,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 100%,#efe3e7,#00000000 50%);width:100%;aspect-ratio:1.537117903930131" srcSet="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=640,f=auto/v1/website/grokbot_messagebuilder_wallpaper_2816x1832-e13f59e2.png 640w,

This Shared Bot supports our Deal Desk team, which reviews exceptions and decides what deal economics and risks the business is willing to accept.</p><p>Deal Bot checks requests against our approved policies and contract language, then prepares the changes needed to move the deal forward. It can also monitor and triage Slack requests submitted by reps, route requests to the right cross-functional owner or approver, and check whether Legal has already drafted similar terms.</p><figure class="not-prose my-12 lg:-mx-12"><div class="bg-card overflow-hidden rounded-2xl"><span class="flex h-full grow"><span role="button" aria-label="Image Preview" class="h-full w-full cursor-pointer"><img alt="Deal Bot and Quote Bot coordinating an order-form revision in Slack after marketing language is removed" class="w-full" loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="object-fit:contain;background:radial-gradient(at 0 0,#ffa391,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 0,#fea388,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 0,#ff9965,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 0,#ffbf9e,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 50%,#fbbfb4,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 50%,#f1d5ce,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 50%,#f8dcd0,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 50%,#fbdace,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 100%,#fec6b5,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 100%,#f1d4ce,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 100%,#f7d8cc,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 100%,#fbdbd1,#00000000 50%);width:100%;aspect-ratio:1.7777777777777777" srcSet="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=640,f=auto/v1/website/slack-deal-2-1-f55e022f.png 640w,

Deal Bot handles much of the routine processing, leaving the Deal Desk team to make the decisions that require commercial expertise and human judgment.</p><figure class="not-prose my-12 lg:-mx-12"><div class="bg-card overflow-hidden rounded-2xl"><span class="flex h-full grow"><span role="button" aria-label="Image Preview" class="h-full w-full cursor-pointer"><img alt="Deal Bot asking a Deal Desk specialist to approve adding already-cleared legal language to a quote&#x27;s special terms" class="w-full" loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="object-fit:contain;background:radial-gradient(at 0 0,#fec8a9,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 0,#f0b596,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 0,#f3b37c,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 0,#e19c7a,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 50%,#f9d3b6,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 50%,#ebe9e2,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 50%,#efe0d2,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 50%,#f0e5e1,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 0 100%,#fad1b1,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 33% 100%,#ecdbd3,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 67% 100%,#f5dfcf,#00000000 50%),radial-gradient(at 100% 100%,#f0dfd7,#00000000 50%);width:100%;aspect-ratio:1.7777777777777777" srcSet="https://media.x.ai/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,onerror=redirect,width=640,f=auto/v1/website/slack-dealbot-2-1-6035cfbe.png 640w,

We&#x27;ve also built Shared Bots like Competitive Intel Bot, which keeps our competitive intelligence current and helps reps prepare for competitive conversations, and Sales Training Bot, which supports employee onboarding and skill development. Across Sales, people are also building and using many more individual Bots for their own work.</p><p>We&#x27;re still early in building out this system. Over time, we expect Shared Bots to take on more responsibilities and coordinate more of their work with one another. Our goal is a sales organization where people can focus on customers while specialized Shared Bots, built and maintained by the people who know each job best, take ownership of much of the work that supports them.</p><div class="not-prose flex flex-col items-center gap-6 text-center mt-20 mb-10 lg:mt-24 lg:mb-12"><h2 class="font-display text-3xl tracking-tight text-balance sm:text-4xl mx-auto
